answers.explanation: Zero Trust's core idea is that network location alone never grants trust. Every request is checked on identity, device, and policy.
Trust by location means one compromised laptop or camera can reach everything its subnet is allowed to reach.
Microsegmentation shrinks the blast radius so a compromise in one segment reaches as little as possible.
Subnets still contain broadcasts and limit the blast radius. Zero Trust stops trusting them; it doesn't throw them away.
Policies written as address ranges are tied to the old boundaries. Miss one and the policy is wrong.
Addresses change and can be spoofed. Identity, with device health and context, is what Zero Trust checks.
Least privilege: no more access than the task needs, for no longer than it needs it.
